analysis.title: JPM Market Intelligence - US Election Series - Midterm Toolkit
key_insights: Options price a ~90bp move in the SPX around the midterms, similar to the average NFP print. JPM equity derivatives strategy puts the implied move at ~0.7% vs 1.1% average realized, so the event is underpriced.
Prediction-market odds as of Nov 1, 2026 (via BBG): Blue Wave (Dem House and Senate) 66%, Split Congress (Dem House, GOP Senate) 26%, Red Wave 7%, GOP House with Dem Senate 1%.

Blue Wave scenario: SPX estimated down 25bp to up 50bp. Trump has said he will not sign bills limiting AI expansion and Democrats cannot reach a veto-proof majority, so AI regulation is hard to enact. The stated risk is de-grossing within the AI theme. Longer-dated bond yields may decline slightly on lower deficit spending. Investigation risk exists for business leaders tied to Trump donations, including MegaCap Tech.

Split Congress (Dem House, GOP Senate): SPX +0.5% to +1%. Deficit spending likely falls and bond yields may decline. Impeachment risk is effectively removed but investigation risk remains. Budget fights are expected in 2027, though shutdowns have limited market impact.
Red Wave: SPX +1% to +1.25% with no new regulatory risk. It may embolden Trump to continue the Iran conflict, and elevated deficit spending may push longer-dated yields higher.
GOP House with Dem Senate: SPX +25bp to +75bp. Budget fights and a possible shutdown are the risks.

Seasonality: SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, averaging about 15%. Average returns are +5.4% at 3 months, 11.4% at 6 months, 12.5% at 9 months and 14.7% at 12 months. The 6, 9 and 12 month returns have a 100% hit rate since 1990.

Historical post-midterm moves: Treasury curves tend to flatten, with 10-year and 30-year sectors leading yields lower. Equities rise initially, but the gains fade after about 8-10 sessions. Nov 2018 was an exception, when tech fell about 3%.

JPM Rates desk: the election is unlikely to be the dominant local market driver. Divided government is the base case, with debt-ceiling and funding confrontation risk and a possible 2027 shutdown. A Democratic sweep raises tech and AI oversight risk, with healthcare and clean energy as possible relative beneficiaries. A Republican sweep implies wider deficits and upward pressure on rates.

JPM Rates and Cross Asset research: no outcome is expected to fundamentally solve the deficit. Michael Feroli does not expect first-order macro implications. Fabio Bassi notes the Fed terminal rate repricing, with cyclicals lagging Tech, lower-quality credit lagging higher-quality credit and high-beta AI lagging Quality AI.
JPMAM view: stay focused on fundamentals, since growth, inflation, earnings, rates and Fed policy matter more than the election itself.

Early voting is up sharply: 43mm votes cast, about 10mm more than in 2022. Texas is up 50%, South Carolina 83%, and Kansas, Maine, Michigan and North Carolina 30%+. Democrats lead in states reporting party affiliation, 6.8mm to 5.2mm Republicans.

Senate math: Democrats must hold Georgia, Michigan, Minnesota and New Hampshire and flip 4 seats, effectively 5 because Fetterman is not expected to stay in the Democratic caucus. Targets are Alaska, Florida, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas. NY Times polls show South Carolina as a statistical tie and Florida within the margin of error.
Texas governor race, data as of Nov 2, 2026: DDHQ GOP +1.6pts, RCP GOP +2.5pts, Polymarket 60.5% and Kalshi 61% for the GOP.

Poll close times: 6PM Indiana and Kentucky (partial), 7PM Georgia, Virginia, South Carolina and most of Florida, 7:30PM North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia, 8PM Texas, Michigan, Kansas, Maine and others, 9PM Minnesota, Iowa and others, midnight Alaska and Hawaii.
Vote counting: many states tabulate within 8 hours of poll close. In 2024 all states except California had at least 75% counted after 48 hours. Alaska, Maine and Michigan tend to report slower.

charts_described: Figure 3 shows SPX implied daily moves over the next month (as of 10/29 close) with key catalyst days labeled and red diamonds marking the average realized move for each event.
vol_and_positioning: SPX options price the midterms as a non-event, with ~0.7% implied vs 1.1% average realized. Near-term vols reset higher after Friday's sharp sell-off, but the midterm implied move was little changed.
Blue Wave risk: the market could use the assumed increase in liquidity to de-gross within the AI theme.
geopolitical: US military engagement in Iran beyond 90 days without Congressional approval. Democrats could pull funding or force troop removal, but only after the new Congress is seated in January.
A Republican sweep may embolden Trump to continue in Iran until a US-friendly deal or Iranian capitulation.
Cross asset strategy flags the risk of geopolitical escalation after the midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: AI regulation is hard to enact because Trump will not sign bills limiting AI expansion and Democrats lack a veto-proof majority. Buy-the-dip opportunity for AI bulls.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic sweep brings tougher AI and tech oversight, possible data-center restrictions and higher corporate taxes. Markets could de-grossing within AI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democrats winning a veto-proof majority in both chambers, which the report treats as not achievable.
